topic.title: The ₹300 cable that could hold your FnF
topic.claim: The scariest part of resigning isn't the notice period, it's returning the laptop and fearing they'll deduct for a taped cable.
topic.behaviour: An employee who has served notice worries that a taped-up charging cable will cause a deduction from their full and final settlement. They are considering buying a cheap aftermarket cable first.
topic.mechanism: The last paycheck is the only leverage the company still holds, and ex-employees know it. Even a tiny item turns into a worry because the power sits entirely on one side, and no one wants to argue over small money with people they just left.
topic.group: salaried employees who are changing jobs
real_details: The employee had finished a notice period
The charging cable was damaged and taped, but still works
The worry is a deduction from FnF
The plan was to buy a cheap aftermarket cable
The poster wanted to know whether this happens all the time
topic.why_now: Appraisal results come out soon, which means a wave of job switching.

score.reason: sharp, specific power-imbalance moment every job-switcher recognises
score.best_hook: The scariest part of quitting isn't the exit interview. It's whether they'll dock your last salary for a taped-up charging cable.
